counting: Total learned parameters, each counted once. Where a weight file stores a tied table twice (FastVLM-1.5B, Ministral 3 3B), params is the unique count and params_upper is the file total.

models.name: Whisper large-v3-turbo
models.paper_title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
models.note: The encoder width is 1280, and the decoder is cut to 4 layers.

details.summary: Whisper large-v3-turbo is an 809M-parameter encoder-decoder Transformer made by pruning large-v3 from 32 decoder layers to 4 and fine-tuning it. Whisper is trained with weak supervision on multilingual, multitask transcription and translation targets.
details.meld_slot: It would transcribe each finished line in either track at close to large-v3 accuracy with a much cheaper decoder.
details.meld_good: It keeps the large-v3 encoder, offers sentence-level and word-level timestamps through Transformers, and its short-form OOD WER is 7.30% against 7.12% for large-v3.
details.meld_weak: It still uses a fixed 30 s receptive field, its card documents hallucination and repeated text, and 809M parameters is heavy for CPU-only real-time use.

scores.text: WER is 2.10% on LibriSpeech clean and 4.24% on LibriSpeech other.
Short-form OOD WER is 7.30% and long-form OOD WER is 10.25%.

details.training_data: Its parent large-v3 was trained on 1M hours of weakly labeled audio and 4M hours pseudo-labeled by large-v2, and turbo is a fine-tuned pruned copy.
details.languages: Its card lists 99 languages, and OpenAI reports strong ASR results in about 10 of them.
details.input_limits: It takes 128-bin log-Mel spectrograms over a 30 s receptive field, and longer audio uses chunked long-form decoding with overlapping 30 s segments.
details.output: It outputs text or an English translation, with optional sentence-level or word-level timestamps.

models.name: EmbeddingGemma-300m
models.paper_title: EmbeddingGemma: Powerful and Lightweight Text Representations
models.note: The Hub total covers only the main weights, and the two Dense projection files add about 4.7M more by file size, which matches the announced 308M.

details.summary: A 300M-parameter text embedding model built on Gemma 3 with T5Gemma encoder-decoder initialization. It is trained with geometric embedding distillation, a spread-out regularizer and Matryoshka representation learning, and the final weights merge checkpoints from several training mixtures.
details.meld_slot: It would be the frozen text encoder for either track, feeding one pooled sentence vector per utterance to the trained head.
details.meld_good: Its 768-d output truncates to 512, 256 or 128 dims through MRL, and the card defines a 'task: classification | query:' prompt for classifier features.
details.meld_weak: Its activations do not support float16, so inference needs fp32 or bf16, and the Hub weights are gated behind acceptance of the Gemma licence.

scores.text: MTEB English v2 mean (task) 69.67 at 768 dims
MTEB Multilingual v2 mean (task) 61.15 at 768 dims

details.training_data: It learned from about 320 billion tokens of web documents, code, technical documentation and synthetic task-specific data.
details.languages: Its training data covers over 100 languages.
details.input_limits: It accepts up to 2,048 tokens of context.
details.output: It returns one L2-normalized 768-d vector from mean pooling plus dense projection layers, and the vector can be truncated to 512, 256 or 128 dims.

models.name: EmoBERTa-large
models.paper_title: EmoBERTa: Speaker-Aware Emotion Recognition in Conversation with RoBERTa
models.note: It was trained on MELD and IEMOCAP, so its MELD test scores are inflated, and the date is the Hub repo's creation date.

details.summary: RoBERTa-large fine-tuned as a seven-class emotion classifier for emotion recognition in conversation. The paper prepends speaker names and adds separator-joined past and future utterances, while the released model classifies one utterance with no speaker or context.
details.meld_slot: It would replace both the text encoder and the head for either track, since it already outputs MELD's seven labels.
details.meld_good: Its labels match MELD's seven classes, and the paper reports MELD wF1 65.61 for the speaker-aware setting with past and future context.
details.meld_weak: It was fine-tuned on MELD and IEMOCAP, so MELD scores are contaminated, and the released single-utterance model does not match the paper's context setup.

scores.text: MELD wF1 65.61 with past and future utterances and speaker names (paper, mean of 5 seeds)
MELD wF1 63.46 with no past or future utterances (paper, mean of 5 seeds)
IEMOCAP wF1 68.57 with past utterances only (paper, mean of 5 seeds)

details.training_data: It was fine-tuned from RoBERTa-large on both MELD and IEMOCAP.
details.languages: English.
details.input_limits: It accepts up to 512 tokens, and the paper fits dialogue context into 512 minus 2 tokens.
details.output: It returns a softmax over neutral, joy, surprise, anger, sadness, disgust and fear from a sequence-classification head on a 1,024-d encoder.

models.name: emotion2vec+ large
models.paper_title: emotion2vec: Self-Supervised Pre-Training for Speech Emotion Representation
models.note: The card says about 300M, but the published checkpoint holds 162.14M model parameters.

details.maker: emotion2vec team (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Alibaba and partners)
details.summary: emotion2vec+ large is the largest emotion2vec+ variant, fine-tuned on 42,526 hours of pseudo-labeled emotion speech after filtering 160,000 candidate hours down to about 40,000. It outputs 9-class emotion scores and frame-level or utterance-level embeddings.
details.meld_slot: It fills the voice-encoder slot on the text and audio track, either as frozen embeddings for the head or as a direct 9-class emotion prior.
details.meld_good: It is trained on the most emotion data in the family, and its 9 classes include all seven MELD labels, so its scores map onto MELD without a new label set.
details.meld_weak: The card reports no benchmark numbers, and its labels were bootstrapped from EmoBox academic corpora, so overlap with MELD or IEMOCAP cannot be ruled out.
details.training_data: It was fine-tuned on 42,526 hours of pseudo-labeled emotion speech, filtered from 160,000 hours and iterated from EmoBox academic emotion data.
details.languages: The card claims universal recognition across languages but does not list the languages of its training data.
details.input_limits: It expects 16 kHz speech, and the card states no maximum length.
details.output: It returns 9 class scores plus optional embeddings, either 50 Hz frames or one utterance vector, and the card does not state the hidden size.

models.name: HuBERT large
models.paper_title: HuBERT: Self-Supervised Speech Representation Learning by Masked Prediction of Hidden Units

details.summary: HuBERT Large is a 24-layer, 1024-dimensional Transformer of about 317M parameters, trained by masked prediction of k-means units. Its targets come from features of the second-iteration Base model, which makes it effectively a third-iteration model.
details.meld_slot: It fills the voice-encoder slot on the text and audio track as a frozen feature extractor under the small trained head.
details.meld_good: As a frozen encoder it scores SUPERB ER 67.62 and SID 90.33, ahead of both wav2vec 2.0 sizes.
details.meld_weak: At 316.61M parameters it still trails WavLM Large on SUPERB ER (67.62 versus 70.62), and it is a pretrain-only English model.

scores.text: SUPERB ER (IEMOCAP 4-class accuracy, frozen, weighted sum of layers) 67.62

details.training_data: It was pre-trained on 60,000 hours of unlabeled Libri-Light English speech.
details.languages: English only.
details.input_limits: It expects 16 kHz audio, and the card states no maximum length.
details.output: It gives 1024-dimensional states from 24 layers at a 20 ms frame rate, and SUPERB pools a learned weighted sum of layers.

models.name: OpenCV YuNet
models.paper_title: YuNet: A Tiny Millisecond-level Face Detector
models.note: The paper reports 75,856 parameters, but the shipped ONNX holds 53,112 float weights, and the newer 2026may file that OpenCV Zoo now defaults to has the same count.

details.summary: A tiny face detector trained on WIDER FACE in the libfacedetection.train pipeline and shipped as ONNX in OpenCV Zoo. Each detection row holds a box, five landmarks and a confidence score.
details.meld_slot: It would find faces in each frame for the vision track, before alignment and expression classification.
details.meld_good: Its five landmarks are the points OpenCV's MobileFaceNet expression model aligns to, and it returns every face in the frame with a score.
details.meld_weak: It detects faces of only about 10 to 300 pixels, so close webcam faces may need downscaling, and it gives no cue about which face is speaking.
details.training_data: It learned from WIDER FACE with labelv2 annotations sourced from SCRFD.
details.languages: Not applicable, since it reads images.
details.input_limits: The demo defaults to 320 by 320, the 2023mar ONNX has a fixed input shape, and the 2026may file has dynamic height and width.
details.output: Each face is 15 values: a 4-value box, five (x, y) landmarks for both eyes, the nose tip and both mouth corners, and a score.

models.name: MediaPipe Face Landmarker
models.paper_title: Real-time Facial Surface Geometry from Monocular Video on Mobile GPUs
models.note: The bundle holds BlazeFace short-range (101,390), Face Mesh V2 (1,199,316) and the blendshape model (450,522), so adding the standalone BlazeFace entry as well would count it twice.

details.summary: A MediaPipe bundle of three models: BlazeFace short-range detection at 192 by 192, a Face Mesh model at 256 by 256, and a blendshape model on a 146-point landmark tensor. It outputs dense 3D face landmarks, 52 blendshape scores and facial transformation matrices.
details.meld_slot: It would find the face and extract a blendshape feature vector for the vision track.
details.meld_good: Its 52 blendshape coefficients form a compact, interpretable expression vector for a small head, and it accepts images, video frames and live streams.
details.meld_weak: num_faces defaults to 1, so MELD's multi-person clips need it raised plus a separate speaker choice, and blendshapes stay off unless output_face_blendshapes is set.
details.languages: Not applicable, since it reads images.
details.input_limits: The bundled detector takes 192 by 192, the mesh model 256 by 256, and the blendshape model a 1 by 146 by 2 landmark tensor, all float16.
details.output: Each face gets 478 3D landmarks, an optional 52-value blendshape vector and an optional facial transformation matrix.

models.name: MediaPipe BlazeFace short-range
models.paper_title: BlazeFace: Sub-millisecond Neural Face Detection on Mobile GPUs
models.note: The model card links arXiv 2006.10204, which is the BlazePose paper, so the BlazeFace arXiv ID is used here instead.

details.summary: A lightweight SSD-style face detector with a feature extractor inspired by MobileNetV1/V2, a GPU-friendly anchor scheme and a tie-resolution step in place of non-maximum suppression. The short-range variant targets selfie and webcam images taken close to the camera.
details.meld_slot: It would find faces in each frame for the vision track, mainly for the live webcam.
details.meld_good: It is built for front-facing phone camera and webcam images, which matches the live single-face case, and the paper reports 200 to 1000+ FPS on flagship devices.
details.meld_weak: It is tuned for short-range framing, so small faces in wide MELD shots may be missed, and its six keypoints do not match the five-point alignment template of OpenCV's FER model.
details.languages: Not applicable, since it reads images.
details.input_limits: It takes 128 by 128 pixel input in float16.
details.output: Each face gets a bounding box and six keypoints: both eyes, the nose tip, the mouth and both ear tragions.

models.name: RetinaFace MobileNet-0.25
models.paper_title: RetinaFace: Single-stage Dense Face Localisation in the Wild
models.note: The count comes from py-feat's Hub mirror of biubug6's mobilenet0.25_Final.pth and excludes 6,735 batch-norm statistics, and the date is that GitHub repo's creation.

details.maker: Jiankang Deng et al. (paper); biubug6 PyTorch port mirrored by py-feat
details.summary: A single-stage dense face detector trained multi-task on boxes, five manually annotated WIDER FACE landmarks and a self-supervised 3D mesh branch. This checkpoint is biubug6's PyTorch port with a MobileNet-0.25 backbone, which the repo lists as a 1.7M model size.
details.meld_slot: It would find faces in each frame for the vision track, and OpenFace 3.0 uses RetinaFace as its own detector.
details.meld_good: It reaches 80.99 hard-set AP at single scale, which helps with small faces in wide multi-person MELD shots, and it returns five alignment landmarks.
details.meld_weak: It returns all faces with no speaker cue, and hard-set AP drops to 73.82 at original image scale, so input scaling needs tuning per source.

scores.text: WIDER FACE val AP easy/medium/hard 88.67/87.09/80.99 at single scale
WIDER FACE val AP easy/medium/hard 90.70/88.16/73.82 at original scale

details.training_data: It learned from WIDER FACE with face-box and five-landmark annotations.
details.languages: Not applicable, since it reads images.
details.input_limits: The repo evaluates at a fixed single scale and at original image scale, and the paper cites real-time single-CPU-core speed on VGA images with light backbones.
details.output: Each face gets a bounding box, a confidence score and five (x, y) landmarks.

models.name: OpenFace 3.0
models.paper_title: OpenFace 3.0: A Lightweight Multitask System for Comprehensive Facial Behavior Analysis
models.note: The 29.4M figure covers the whole system (RetinaFace detector, landmark model, and an emotion, action-unit and gaze backbone), the paper gives no feature size, and the license allows only noncommercial research.

details.maker: CMU MultiComp Lab (Hu, Mathur, Liang and Morency)
details.summary: A facial behavior toolkit that chains RetinaFace detection, STAR landmarks and one multitask model with an EfficientNet backbone pretrained on VGGFace2. The multitask model predicts eight AffectNet emotions, action-unit intensities and gaze yaw and pitch.
details.meld_slot: It would cover face finding and expression features for the vision track in one package.
details.meld_good: Action-unit intensities and gaze add detail beyond class labels, and the paper reports 38 ms per frame on CPU for the whole 29.4M-parameter system.
details.meld_weak: Its licence allows only academic or non-profit noncommercial research, and its eight classes include contempt, which MELD lacks.
details.training_data: It learned emotion from AffectNet, action units from DISFA and BP4D, gaze from MPII Gaze and Gaze360, and landmarks from 300W and WFLW.
details.languages: Not applicable, since it reads images.
details.input_limits: The paper states no input resolution, and the toolkit takes image files such as JPEGs.
details.output: Each face gets 2D landmarks, eight emotion scores, AU intensities and gaze yaw and pitch, and the paper gives no feature-vector size.

models.name: OpenCV MobileFaceNet expression model
models.paper_title: Boosting Facial Expression Recognition by A Semi-Supervised Progressive Teacher
models.note: It predicts seven expressions with 88.27% reported accuracy on RAF-DB, and it expects faces aligned with YuNet's five landmarks.

details.maker: Jing Jiang and Weihong Deng (method); OpenCV Zoo (packaging)
details.summary: A MobileFaceNet expression classifier trained with Progressive Teacher, a semi-supervised method that selects clean labeled samples and adds a consistency loss on unlabeled faces. OpenCV Zoo ships it as ONNX for seven basic expressions.
details.meld_slot: It would classify the aligned speaker face into expression scores for the vision track.
details.meld_good: Its seven classes map one to one onto MELD's labels, it is Apache 2.0, and an int8 block-quantized ONNX variant exists for CPU use.
details.meld_weak: It expects a 112 by 112 face aligned to five reference points, so it depends on YuNet-style landmarks, and the card names no training dataset.

scores.text: RAF-DB accuracy 89.57% (paper's best Progressive Teacher result)

details.training_data: The card names no dataset, and the paper combines labeled FER datasets with large-scale unlabeled face images and evaluates on RAF-DB and FERPlus.
details.languages: Not applicable, since it reads images.
details.input_limits: It takes 112 by 112 pixels after alignment to five reference points.
details.output: It returns seven class scores for angry, disgust, fearful, happy, neutral, sad and surprised.

models.name: ViT face-expression
models.note: It has no paper and is google/vit-base-patch16-224-in21k fine-tuned on FER2013 with 71.16% reported test accuracy, and the date is the Hub repo's first commit.

details.summary: A ViT-Base/16 classifier, google/vit-base-patch16-224-in21k pretrained on ImageNet-21k, fine-tuned on FER2013 for seven facial expressions. Training used resizing, normalization and random rotation, flip and zoom augmentation.
details.meld_slot: It would classify the cropped speaker face into expression scores for the vision track.
details.meld_good: Its seven classes match MELD's after renaming, such as angry to anger and happy to joy, and it reached 71.16% FER2013 test accuracy.
details.meld_weak: As a ViT-Base with 768-d hidden states it is heavy for a per-frame face model, it has no paper, and the card warns that generalization depends on FER2013's diversity.
details.training_data: It was fine-tuned on FER2013.
details.languages: Not applicable, since it reads images.
details.input_limits: It takes 224 by 224 pixels split into 16 by 16 patches.
details.output: It returns seven class scores for angry, disgust, fear, happy, neutral, sad and surprise from a 768-d ViT.

models.name: HSEmotion enet_b2_8
models.paper_title: Classifying emotions and engagement in online learning based on a single facial expression recognition neural network
models.note: The README lists it at 30 MB with 191 ms inference time, against 16 MB and 59 ms for enet_b0.

details.summary: An EfficientNet-B2 facial expression model pretrained for face identification on VGGFace2 and fine-tuned on AffectNet for eight emotions. It ships in EmotiEffLib, formerly HSEmotion, with Python and C++ support.
details.meld_slot: It would classify the cropped speaker face, or hand its embedding to the head, for the vision track.
details.meld_good: It is the more accurate of the two HSEmotion entries on AffectNet, extract_features() exposes its embedding, and Apache 2.0 allows commercial use.
details.meld_weak: Its 260 by 260 input makes it about three times slower than enet_b0 (191 against 59 ms), and its eight classes include contempt, which MELD lacks.
details.training_data: It was pretrained for face identification on VGGFace2, then fine-tuned for expressions on AffectNet.
details.languages: Not applicable, since it reads images.
details.input_limits: It takes 260 by 260 pixels.
details.output: It returns eight class scores (anger, contempt, disgust, fear, happiness, neutral, sadness, surprise) or an EfficientNet feature vector.

models.name: HSEmotion enet_b0_8_best_afew
models.paper_title: Classifying emotions and engagement in online learning based on a single facial expression recognition neural network
models.note: The file was re-uploaded in 2022-08 and 2023-09 for newer timm versions, and the repo has moved from av-savchenko/face-emotion-recognition to sb-ai-lab/EmotiEffLib.

details.summary: An EfficientNet-B0 facial expression model pretrained for face identification on VGGFace2 and fine-tuned on AffectNet for eight emotions. This best_afew checkpoint scores 59.89% on AFEW, above enet_b2_8, and ships in EmotiEffLib.
details.meld_slot: It would classify the cropped speaker face, or hand its embedding to the head, for the vision track.
details.meld_good: At 224 by 224 and 59 ms per face it is about three times faster than enet_b2_8, it beats that model on AFEW, and Apache 2.0 allows commercial use.
details.meld_weak: It gives up about two points of AffectNet accuracy against enet_b2_8, and its eight classes include contempt, which MELD lacks.
details.training_data: It was pretrained for face identification on VGGFace2, then fine-tuned for expressions on AffectNet.
details.languages: Not applicable, since it reads images.
details.input_limits: It takes 224 by 224 pixels.
details.output: It returns eight class scores (anger, contempt, disgust, fear, happiness, neutral, sadness, surprise) or an EfficientNet feature vector.

models.name: DINOv3 ViT-S/16
models.paper_title: DINOv3
models.note: The repo is gated and uses Meta's custom DINOv3 License rather than Apache-2.0.

details.summary: DINOv3 ViT-S/16 is a 21M-parameter Vision Transformer with 16-pixel patches, pretrained without labels by self-supervised learning plus Gram anchoring, which stops dense patch features from degrading over long training. Meta presents its features as usable frozen, without fine-tuning.
details.meld_slot: It would turn face crops into frozen vectors for the text and vision track, one frame at a time.
details.meld_good: Its 21M parameters and 201 output tokens per 224-pixel image keep per-frame cost low, and the frozen CLS vector can feed a small trained head directly.
details.meld_weak: The weights are gated under Meta's custom DINOv3 License, it reads single frames only, and no facial-expression result is reported, so expression sensitivity is unmeasured.
details.training_data: It learned without labels from 1,689 million web images selected from a pool of 17 billion public Instagram images.
details.languages: Not applicable, it reads images only.
details.input_limits: It takes 224 by 224 pixel images by default and accepts larger sizes that are multiples of the 16-pixel patch.
details.output: It outputs 201 tokens of width 384 per 224-pixel image: one CLS token, four register tokens and 196 patch tokens.

models.name: V-JEPA 2 ViT-L
models.paper_title: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning
models.note: The total includes a 22,086,016-parameter predictor that feature extraction does not use, which leaves 303,885,312 for the encoder.

details.summary: V-JEPA 2 ViT-L/16 is a 300M-parameter video Vision Transformer pretrained self-supervised with a joint-embedding predictive objective, which trains a separate 12-layer predictor over masked tokens. Meta pretrained it on over one million hours of internet video plus images.
details.meld_slot: Its encoder would turn short face clips into vectors for the text and vision track, capturing motion across frames.
details.meld_good: It models motion across frames and reaches 73.7% on SSv2 with a frozen attentive probe, which suits expressions that unfold over an utterance.
details.meld_weak: A full 64-frame clip at 256 pixels becomes 8,192 tokens through 24 layers of width 1024, which is heavy on CPU, and no facial-expression result is reported.
details.training_data: It was pretrained without labels on over one million hours of internet video combined with image data.
details.languages: Not applicable, it reads images only.
details.input_limits: It takes clips of up to 64 frames at 256 by 256 pixels, cut into tubelets of 2 frames by 16 by 16 pixels.
details.output: It outputs one 1024-wide token per tubelet, which is 8,192 tokens for a full 64-frame clip, so a probe or pooling step must reduce them to one vector.

models.name: SigLIP 2 base patch16-224
models.paper_title: SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features
models.note: The vision tower alone is 92,884,224 parameters, and the text tower with its 256,000-token vocabulary is the other 282,303,744.

details.summary: SigLIP 2 B/16 is a dual image-text encoder trained with SigLIP's pairwise sigmoid loss plus earlier, independently developed techniques for better semantics, localization and dense features. It pairs a ViT-B/16 image tower with a multilingual text tower that uses the 256k-token Gemma tokenizer.
details.meld_slot: Its image tower would turn face crops into vectors for the text and vision track, and the text tower would go unused.
details.meld_good: It beats SigLIP B/16 on every Table 1 benchmark at the same 196 patch tokens per 224-pixel image, so the upgrade costs no extra compute per frame.
details.meld_weak: The checkpoint carries a 256k-vocabulary text tower that a face pipeline never uses, it reads single frames only, and no facial-expression result is reported.
details.training_data: It learned from WebLI image-text pairs, 90% from English web pages and 10% from non-English pages, with de-biasing techniques in the mix.
details.languages: Its text tower is multilingual, trained with 10% non-English pairs and the Gemma tokenizer, and the paper does not list the languages.
details.input_limits: It takes 224 by 224 pixel images and text of up to 64 tokens.
details.output: It outputs one image embedding built from 196 patch tokens and one text embedding, scored against each other with a sigmoid; the card does not state the width.

models.name: VideoMAE-base
models.paper_title: VideoMAE: Masked Autoencoders are Data-Efficient Learners for Self-Supervised Video Pre-Training
models.note: This is the self-supervised pretraining checkpoint, whose encoder alone is 86,227,200 parameters, and its license bars commercial use.

details.summary: VideoMAE-base is a ViT-B video masked autoencoder that cuts a 16-frame clip into tubelets of 2 frames by 16 by 16 pixels, masks some, and trains a light 4-layer decoder to predict their pixels. This checkpoint is the self-supervised pretraining model, not a classifier.
details.meld_slot: Its encoder would turn short face clips into vectors for the text and vision track.
details.meld_good: It reads 16-frame clips, so it can encode motion, and ViT-B fine-tuned from this pretraining reaches 81.5% top-1 on Kinetics-400 with no extra data.
details.meld_weak: Its config turns mean pooling off and its head predicts pixels, so a probe must learn the pooling, and the CC-BY-NC-4.0 licence bars commercial use.

scores.text: Kinetics-400 top-1 81.5% and top-5 95.1% after fine-tuning ViT-B from 1,600-epoch pretraining

details.training_data: It was pretrained without labels on Kinetics-400 for 1,600 epochs.
details.languages: Not applicable, it reads images only.
details.input_limits: It takes 16 frames at 224 by 224 pixels, cut into tubelets of 2 frames by 16 by 16 pixels.
details.output: Its encoder outputs 1,568 tokens of width 768 per clip, and this checkpoint's decoder head predicts masked pixel values.

models.name: Swin-Tiny
models.paper_title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows
models.note: The total includes the 769,000-parameter ImageNet-1K classifier, and the Hub card says Apache-2.0 while the GitHub repo is MIT.

details.summary: Swin-T is a hierarchical Vision Transformer that computes self-attention inside shifted 7 by 7 windows and merges patches between stages, so its cost grows linearly with image size. This checkpoint is trained with labels on ImageNet-1k and carries a 1,000-class head.
details.meld_slot: Its backbone would turn face crops into vectors for the text and vision track once the classifier is dropped.
details.meld_good: It is cheap at 28M parameters, 4.5 GFLOPs and 755 images per second as reported, and its hierarchical feature maps suit fine-tuning on face crops.
details.meld_weak: Its features come from supervised ImageNet-1k object labels rather than large-scale pretraining, it reads single frames, and no facial-expression result is reported.

scores.text: ImageNet-1k top-1 81.2% and top-5 95.5% at 224 pixels

details.training_data: It was trained with labels on ImageNet-1k.
details.languages: Not applicable, it reads images only.
details.input_limits: It takes 224 by 224 pixel images, with 4-pixel patches and 7 by 7 attention windows.
details.output: It outputs 1,000 ImageNet logits, and with the head removed it gives final-stage features from stages of depth 2, 2, 6 and 2 on a 96-channel base.

models.name: TimeSformer-base
models.paper_title: Is Space-Time Attention All You Need for Video Understanding?
models.note: The total includes a 307,600-parameter Kinetics-400 classifier, and its license bars commercial use.

details.summary: TimeSformer-base is a convolution-free video ViT that uses divided space-time attention, applying temporal and spatial self-attention separately in each block. This checkpoint is fine-tuned on Kinetics-400 and classifies 8-frame clips into 400 actions.
details.meld_slot: Its encoder would turn short face clips into vectors for the text and vision track once the action classifier is dropped.
details.meld_good: It models motion across 8 frames with 768-wide tokens, and it reaches 77.9% top-1 on Kinetics-400 at 224 pixels.
details.meld_weak: Its features are fine-tuned for Kinetics-400 action classes rather than faces, and the CC-BY-NC-4.0 licence bars commercial use.

scores.text: Kinetics-400 top-1 77.9% and top-5 93.2% with 8 frames at 224 pixels

details.training_data: It was fine-tuned with labels on the Kinetics-400 action dataset, and the card does not describe its pretraining.
details.languages: Not applicable, it reads images only.
details.input_limits: It takes 8 frames at 224 by 224 pixels with 16-pixel patches.
